verdict.rationale: SES documents a getting-started path that is upfront about required setup: verify an email address and sending domain first, and while the account is in the sandbox you can only send to verified identities. Sending works through SDKs, SMTP or the API. However, the sandbox and production-access step slow down 'minutes to first delivered email', and new users report first emails landing in spam until extra configuration (e.g. reverse PTR) is fixed. Missing for 10: evidence of copy-paste-complete per-language quickstart code, a sub-minutes path past sandbox restrictions, and hands-on corroboration of a fast first successful send.
